text: Yolcu’s constitutional-adjudication study documents a functionally separated institutional arrangement: the Venice Commission supplies non-binding comparative-law advice, while the requesting constitutional court retains the determination whether the statute complies with the constitution. That arrangement independently extends Kaal’s role-separation design by showing how an advisory signal can inform reasoning without acquiring binding authority. The match is limited to constitutional adjudication; it does not validate Kaal’s agent-pool implementation or establish that separation alone guarantees independence.
